findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the helper's exact cast command by citing the pinned action's source/tag (or an executed transcript) for the `--label Verified=<vote>` / `--message` / `--tag` form, rather than asserting it matches an opaque external action the repo cannot confirm.
evidence: Plan: 'runs the same SSH key/known_hosts material, runs the same `gerrit review <change>,<patchset> --message "<STATUS>: <run URL>" --label Verified=<vote> --tag autogenerated:github` command'
gerrit-verify.yaml:504-522 cast uses external action with only vote-type input
search_files 'autogenerated:github' → only gerrit-verify.yaml:612 (the comment step)
search_files 'Verified=' → no `--label Verified=` cast form anywhere in repo
gerrit-verify.yaml:519-521: 'The action exposes NO input for custom message text ...' — the exact vote message/label is the action's internal composition
findings.finding: The plan asserts the helper will run 'the same ... gerrit review <change>,<patchset> --message "<STATUS>: <run URL>" --label Verified=<vote> --tag autogenerated:github command', but this exact cast command is the internal behavior of the opaque pinned third-party action lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action@a1c036a. A repo grep shows the cast's --label Verified= and --tag autogenerated:github appear nowhere in the codebase (the only autogenerated:github tag is on the separate comment-only step, gerrit-verify.yaml:612), and the workflow's own inline comment (lines 516-521) attests only the --message run-URL shape, not the --label/--tag. The command the helper must replicate is thus unverifiable from the repo.
scenarios: Helper reconstructs the cast command with a different label expression or tag than the action actually used, silently changing the vote or message on the live change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC4 with tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py — that suite currently pins the cast step via the literal `gerrit-review-action` uses: string (lines 64/74/108); state that these assertions must be rewritten to recognize the new repo helper, since they do not yet validate a 'default-branch helper' as claimed.
evidence: AC4: 'proves the vote job uses the default-branch helper, consumes the normalized vote type ...'
test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py:64 `cast = _step(steps, "gerrit-review-action")`
test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py:73-75 `casts = [s for s in steps if "gerrit-review-action" in str(s.get("uses", ""))]; assert len(casts) == 1`
test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py:108 `cast_index = next(... "gerrit-review-action" in n)`
findings.finding: AC4 claims tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py 'proves the vote job uses the default-branch helper', but as written that test file locates and pins the cast step by the literal external-action string 'gerrit-review-action' (test at lines 64, 74, 108) and test_only_one_step_casts_a_vote asserts exactly one `uses: gerrit-review-action` step. Replacing that invocation with a repo helper (per the Plan) makes those assertions FALSE unless the test is rewritten — yet the plan treats the existing suite as already validating a 'helper'. The premise that this test currently validates a default-branch helper is refuted by the file.
scenarios: Author runs AC4's pytest expecting a pass but the existing assertions still key on the removed external action, breaking the suite; or author edits tests to match without the plan flagging it as required work

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reference bug c943 (voter.py 409-terminal handling) as the prior art for the closed-change disposition and state whether the CI leg's exit-0 branch should mirror its skip-recording / error-suppression semantics.
evidence: voter.py:644-657 already treats a 409 'change is closed' as TERMINAL (record + do NOT increment voter_errors) because the change merged/abandoned past an open-status filter — 'A 409 "change is closed" is TERMINAL, not a retryable failure … bug c943'
infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:459 'Voter errors — 409 "change is closed" (bug c943)' documents the same race and resolution
CHANGELOG.md:567 'Treat 409 "change is closed" as terminal + document c943 disposition'

Plan proposes: 'If Gerrit output contains `fatal: change is closed` … exit 0 because the change has already moved to a terminal unvoteable state' — the same disposition, but with no cross-reference to c943 or its recording/metric decisions
findings.finding: The plan applies a 'change is closed = benign terminal skip' disposition to the CI Verified vote leg without referencing the directly-analogous internal prior art (bug c943), which already established that exact disposition for the review-bot LLM-Review vote leg.
findings.location: Plan section: Root cause / Plan (the 'fatal: change is closed' -> exit 0 branch)
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer cannot tell whether the CI leg's closed-change handling is intentionally consistent with the review-bot leg's c943 handling

The two handlers diverge over time (e.g. one records a skip disposition / suppresses an error counter, the other silently exits 0) making incident triage of 'change is closed' inconsistent across the two vote paths
findings.suggested_fix: In Root cause / Plan, cite c943 and note that this extends the same 'closed-change race = benign terminal, not a fault' disposition already applied in src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py to the CI Verified vote leg, calling out any intentional difference (the CI leg has no dedup store, so it only emits a notice).

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note the existing raw-ssh `gerrit review` step (gerrit-verify.yaml:574-612) as the pattern to reuse/align with, and state how the new helper's SSH install and change/patchset integer guard match it.
evidence: .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:574-612 already runs a raw ssh gerrit review: it writes GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY/known_hosts, runs `ssh -i … -p 29418 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -- <user>@<server> gerrit review <change>,<patchset> --message … --tag autogenerated:github`, and guards change/patchset with `^[1-9][0-9]*$`

Plan text: 'The helper installs the same SSH key/known_hosts material, runs the same `gerrit review <change>,<patchset> … --tag autogenerated:github` command' — describes materially the same raw-ssh setup with no reference to the existing step's SSH install / integer-guard pattern
findings.finding: The plan proposes a new 'trusted repo helper' that installs SSH key/known_hosts and runs a raw `gerrit review` command without noting that the same workflow already contains a raw-ssh gerrit-review step it could reuse or align with.
findings.location: Plan section: Plan (the 'trusted repo helper checked out from the default branch' paragraph)
scenarios: The new helper's SSH setup, host-key checking, or change/patchset validation drifts from the existing triage-comment step's proven pattern
Duplicate SSH-material handling increases the surface where the vote key could be mishandled relative to the already-reviewed pattern
findings.suggested_fix: In the Plan section, reference the 'Post the triage detail to Gerrit' step as prior art and specify that the new cast helper reuses its SSH key/known_hosts install approach, `-p 29418 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, and `^[1-9][0-9]*$` change/patchset guard so the two raw-ssh paths stay consistent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the closed-change classification matches the anchored Gerrit error line (e.g. a line equal to `fatal: change is closed`), not any substring occurrence, and add/adjust a test asserting an unrelated failure merely containing that phrase still fails closed.
evidence: "If Gerrit output contains `fatal: change is closed`, print an Actions notice ... and exit 0"
VERIFY-COMMAND DEFECT TAXONOMY item (1) substring false-positive
findings.finding: The closed-change classification keys on the presence of the substring `fatal: change is closed` in Gerrit output, but the plan does not specify whether the match is anchored to the actual Gerrit error line versus any occurrence (e.g. echoed in the review message or a partial line), risking a substring false-positive that swallows a real failure whose output happens to contain that phrase.
scenarios: A different Gerrit failure whose stderr embeds the phrase (or a message argument that repeats it) is misclassified as a benign noop and silently exits 0
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact match semantics in the plan (anchor to the stderr error line) and note the corresponding assertion in test_other_vote_failures_still_fail.
